Subject: Security questionnaire: PII handling + dataflow (DataShield request)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our vendor onboarding we need a short security/privacy Q&A and supporting artifacts focused on PII handling and data transfers. Attached is our short questionnaire (DataShield_Security_QA_v2.pdf). High-level asks:

- A current data flow diagram that shows where PII enters the system, transient caches, and any persistent stores.
- A list of subprocessors and their data access scopes (including any cloud infra partners).
- Clarification on KMS/keys: who holds keys in hosted vs private deployments, and any third parties with key access.
- Cross-border transfer controls (use of SCCs, role of customer-controlled regions).
- Typical retention and deletion behavior for transcripts/logs when a customer opts-in to persist data.

Can you please confirm whether you can provide the diagram and subprocessor matrix within 3 business days, and if you have a SOC 2 or equivalent attestation we can review?

Best,
Amelie Rousseau

Subject: Re: Fwd: Security questionnaire: PII handling + dataflow (DataShield request)

Olga / Laura — technical answers below. I'm attaching the current diagram and our subprocessor matrix for review.

Summary answers (draft):
- Data classification: We treat fields marked as PII by the customer as "sensitive". By default, hosted API requests are ephemeral: tokenized model processing uses in-memory KV cache on GPUs and nothing persists to disk except optional customer-requested logs. For Dedicated/Private, persistent storage depends on customer configuration (e.g., log retention enabled).

- Data flow highlight (see attached redwood_dataflow_v3.png):
  * Ingest: customer -> edge gateway (TLS 1.2+/mTLS for Dedicated)
  * Router: policy-based routing (region/tier) -> runtime cluster
  * Runtime: in-memory KV cache for decoding; ephemeral blobs exist only for request window.
  * Optional persistence: if customer enables logging or evaluation, artifacts are written to object storage (S3) in the customer-selected region.

- Subprocessors: attached subprocessor_matrix.csv. Short list: AWS (in specific regions), GCP (for certain customers), CloudGPU vendor partner (NVIDIA Cloud/GPU partners), monitoring provider (Datadog for hosted telemetry). For Private deployments, the customer often restricts subprocessors to their own infra.

- KMS/key custody:
  * Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood-managed keys by default (AWS KMS). Customers can request customer-keyed encryption for sensitive workloads — we support customer-managed CMKs (bring-your-own-key) via KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private.
  * Private: by default, keys are customer-managed and can be integrated with the customer's KMS/HSM.
  * No third party has key access in Private deployments; in hosted, key material is not exported to partners — we operate with standard KMS APIs.

- Cross-border transfers / SCCs: We support region routing and can commit to SCCs for EU customers. We do not apply blanket international replication for hosted customer data unless customer opts into multi-region replication.

- Retention/deletion: Default retention for hosted is transient (no persistent logs). If customer enables persistence, retention is configurable by contract; we support deletion requests and provide audit logs for deletion operations.

Attachments: redwood_dataflow_v3.png (diagram), subprocessor_matrix.csv (matrix with access scopes).

Let me know if Laura needs any additional technical attestations for the DPA redline.

— Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood_dataflow_v3.png; subprocessor_matrix.csv

Thanks Marcus — this is good. A few legal items before we send back to DataShield: 

- SCCs/DPA: We can commit to SCCs for transfers from the EU; I'll attach a redline of our standard DPA with a clause clarifying customer-controlled region routing and KMS options. See attached DPA_redline_v1.pdf.
- SOC 2: We can provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. Recommend we ask for a mutual NDA link or secure sharing channel (their portal or our Confluence attachments).
- KMS attestation: Marcus, Laura (typo corrected — Laura to Marcus: please provide a short bullet list confirming that hosted keys are not exported and that CMK support exists for Dedicated). I will include that wording in the DPA.

Plan: consolidate Marcus's technical bullets into the response PDF, attach the diagram and subprocessor matrix, include the DPA redline, and route to Amelie with an ask for a secure upload for SOC 2. Olga — happy for you to send once Marcus confirms the two KMS bullets below.

KMS bullets for DPA:
1) "Redwood-managed keys are used by default for hosted deployments; key material is not exported and is managed via our cloud KMS integrations."
2) "Customer-managed keys (CMKs) are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; in Private, keys can be fully customer-controlled and integrated with their KMS/HSM."

Laura Bennett

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Amelie Rousseau <amelie.rousseau@datashield.co>, legal@datashield.co
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: PII handling + dataflow (DataShield request)

Hi Amelie — thanks for the questionnaire and for your patience. Please find our consolidated responses and artifacts attached. Highlights below and attachments in the bundle: Redwood_Response_QA_20270621.pdf (consolidated answers), redwood_dataflow_v3.png ( annotated dataflow), subprocessor_matrix.csv, and a redline of our standard DPA (DPA_redline_v1.pdf). We have also included links for secure exchange: Confluence evidence bundle and a DocuSign link to begin DPA signature if the redline looks acceptable.

Key points: 
- Data flow & persistence: By default, hosted API requests are processed in-memory and are ephemeral; persistent storage is only used when customers explicitly enable logging/retention. The attached diagram shows the request path and persistence points.
- Subprocessors: See CSV for the list and scopes; we can provide region-limited subprocessors for EU customers where required.
- KMS and key custody: Redwood-managed keys are used by default for hosted deployments; key material is not exported and is managed via our cloud KMS integrations. Customer-managed keys (CMKs) are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; in Private, keys can be fully customer-controlled and integrated with their KMS/HSM.
- Cross-border transfers: We support region routing and SCCs; we do not replicate customer data internationally unless configured to do so.
- Evidence: We can provide SOC 2 Type II under NDA — please let us know your preferred secure upload mechanism.

Attachments: Redwood_Response_QA_20270621.pdf; redwood_dataflow_v3.png; subprocessor_matrix.csv; DPA_redline_v1.pdf

Confluence evidence folder: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/DataShield+Evidence+Bundle
DocuSign DPA link: https://www.docusign.com/DocuSign/link-for-DataShield-DPA-20270621

If you want to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the diagram and KMS options, happy to schedule with Marcus and Laura.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
